title: Probes, Health Checks and API Deprecations

header.html: Implement probes and health checks; Understand API deprecations

html:
1Three probes, three questions

The kubelet checks the health of a container with probes. A container is "running" as soon as its process starts; that says nothing about whether the app works.

Probe Question What a failure does
Startup has the app finished starting? after failureThreshold failures the container is restarted; the other probes are paused until it succeeds
Readiness can the app take traffic now? the Pod is removed from the Service endpoints (not restarted); it returns when the probe passes
Liveness is the app still alive? the container is restarted

Liveness is for apps that hang. Readiness is for apps that start slowly, warm a cache, or lose a dependency for a while. A slow starter needs a startup probe, so that the liveness probe does not kill it during start.

2Probe mechanisms

Mechanism Passes when Example
httpGet the response status is 200 to 399 httpGet: {path: /healthz, port: 8080}
tcpSocket the TCP connection opens tcpSocket: {port: 5432}
exec the command exits with 0 exec: {command: ["cat", "/tmp/healthy"]}
grpc the gRPC health check answers SERVING grpc: {port: 9090} 
containers:
- name: app
  image: nginx:alpine
  startupProbe:
    httpGet: {path: /, port: 80}
    periodSeconds: 5
    failureThreshold: 12        # up to 60 seconds to start
  readinessProbe:
    httpGet: {path: /, port: 80}
    initialDelaySeconds: 3
    periodSeconds: 5
  livenessProbe:
    httpGet: {path: /, port: 80}
    periodSeconds: 10
    failureThreshold: 3
Field Meaning Default
initialDelaySeconds wait before the first probe 0
periodSeconds how often to probe 10
timeoutSeconds how long one probe may take 1
successThreshold passes in a row to count as success (must be 1 for liveness and startup) 1
failureThreshold failures in a row to count as failed 3

A liveness probe that is too strict (a 1-second timeout on a slow app, a check of a dependency) causes restart loops. Make the liveness check cheap and local. Probes are set per container; you cannot change them on a running Pod: edit the Deployment (Pods are replaced) or recreate the Pod.

3Reading probe failures

k describe pod web            # Events: "Readiness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 404"
k get pods                    # READY 0/1 with STATUS Running: readiness failing
k get pods -w                 # RESTARTS grows: liveness (or the app) failing
k get endpoints web           # empty ADDRESSES: no Ready Pod behind the Service
k logs web --previous         # log of the container before the last restart

Running and 0/1 Ready means the readiness probe fails; Running with a rising RESTARTS means liveness (or a crashing app). Fix the probe path, port or timing, or the app.

Exam tip

. A new Deployment whose Pods stay 0/1 for ever, with a probe on /healthz for a web server that serves only /, is a classic "fix the probe" task. Check the real path with k exec <pod> -- wget -qO- localhost/.

4API versions and deprecations

Every object has an apiVersion made of a group and a version: apps/v1, batch/v1, networking.k8s.io/v1; the core group is just v1. A version moves through stages:

Stage Name looks like Meaning
Alpha v1alpha1 off by default; may change or vanish
Beta v1beta1 on or off by default; may change
Stable (GA) v1 kept for a long time

When a stable version replaces a beta version, the old one is deprecated (still served, with a warning) and later removed: a manifest that uses it fails with no matches for kind "CronJob" in version "batch/v1beta1". Famous removals: extensions/v1beta1 and apps/v1beta1 Deployments, networking.k8s.io/v1beta1 Ingress (removed in 1.22), batch/v1beta1 CronJob and policy/v1beta1 PodDisruptionBudget (removed in 1.25), autoscaling/v2beta2 HPA (removed in 1.26).

Find the version the cluster serves:

k api-versions | grep -E "batch|policy|networking"      # every group/version served
k api-resources | grep -iE "cronjob|ingress|poddisruption"   # NAME ... APIVERSION NAMESPACED KIND
k explain cronjob | head -4                              # header shows GROUP, KIND, VERSION
k explain ingress.spec.rules --api-version=networking.k8s.io/v1

Fix an old manifest. Change apiVersion, then apply what the new schema requires. For apps/v1, spec.selector is required and must match the Pod template labels (the beta versions defaulted it). For networking.k8s.io/v1 Ingress, pathType is required and the backend is service: {name, port: {number}}. Run k apply --dry-run=server -f file.yaml to check without creating.

Warnings. kubectl prints Warning: ... is deprecated when you use a deprecated API; the API server also exports metrics for deprecated calls. kubectl convert is a separate plugin and is not part of the standard install, so do not count on it.

Exam tip

. For "this manifest fails", read the first line of the error: it names the kind and the version. Use k api-resources to get the right apiVersion, then fix the fields the new version needs.

5Lab tasks

<!-- LABS: m07 -->

Lab 7.1: liveness exec

Domain: Observability | Points: 6 | Time: about 7 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m07-01-liveness-exec)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

The Pod live in the namespace probes (manifest ~/work/live.yaml) creates the file /tmp/healthy, deletes it after 15 seconds and keeps running. Add a liveness probe to its container that runs the command cat /tmp/healthy every 3 seconds (periodSeconds: 3) and treats 2 failures in a row as failed (failureThreshold: 2). Recreate the Pod from the corrected manifest. The kubelet must then restart the container at least once.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n probes delete pod live --wait=true
cat > ~/work/live.yaml <<'Y'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: live
  namespace: probes
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sh", "-c", "touch /tmp/healthy; sleep 15; rm -f /tmp/healthy; sleep 3600"]
    livenessProbe:
      exec:
        command: ["cat", "/tmp/healthy"]
      periodSeconds: 3
      failureThreshold: 2
Y
kubectl apply -f ~/work/live.yaml
for i in $(seq 1 30); do [ "$(kubectl -n probes get pod live -o jsonpath='{.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount}')" -ge 1 ] 2>/dev/null && break; sleep 3; done
kubectl -n probes describe pod live | grep -i -A2 "Liveness"

Lab 7.2: fix readiness path

Domain: Observability | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m07-02-fix-readiness-path)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace probes, the Pods of the Deployment web (2 replicas of nginx:alpine, which serves its page at /) never become Ready, because the readiness probe checks a path that does not exist. Fix the Deployment so that the readiness probe is an HTTP GET on path / and port 80, keep the probe, and wait until both replicas are Ready.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n probes describe pod -l app=web | grep -i "readiness"
kubectl -n probes patch deployment web --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/readinessProbe/httpGet/path","value":"/"}]'
kubectl -n probes rollout status deployment web --timeout=120s

Lab 7.3: startup probe

Domain: Observability | Points: 7 | Time: about 8 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m07-03-startup-probe)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

The Pod slow in the namespace probes (manifest ~/work/slow.yaml) needs about 25 seconds to start, but its liveness probe starts checking after 1 second and keeps killing it. Without removing or loosening the liveness probe, add a startup probe to the container that runs the same command test -f /tmp/started every 5 seconds with failureThreshold: 12, so that the liveness probe only begins after the app has started. Recreate the Pod from the corrected manifest. It must become Ready with restartCount 0.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n probes delete pod slow --wait=true
cat > ~/work/slow.yaml <<'Y'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: slow
  namespace: probes
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 25; touch /tmp/started; sleep 3600"]
    startupProbe:
      exec:
        command: ["sh", "-c", "test -f /tmp/started"]
      periodSeconds: 5
      failureThreshold: 12
    livenessProbe:
      exec:
        command: ["sh", "-c", "test -f /tmp/started"]
      initialDelaySeconds: 1
      periodSeconds: 2
      failureThreshold: 2
Y
kubectl apply -f ~/work/slow.yaml
kubectl -n probes wait --for=condition=Ready pod/slow --timeout=120s
kubectl -n probes get pod slow

Lab 7.4: probe types

Domain: Observability | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m07-04-probe-types)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace probes, create a Pod named api with one container (image nginx:alpine) that has a readiness probe of type TCP socket on port 80 (initialDelaySeconds: 3, periodSeconds: 5) and a liveness probe of type HTTP GET on path / and port 80 (periodSeconds: 10, failureThreshold: 3). Wait until the Pod is Ready.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n probes run api --image=nginx:alpine --dry-run=client -o yaml > /tmp/api.yaml
sed -i 's/^    resources: {}/    readinessProbe:\n      tcpSocket: {port: 80}\n      initialDelaySeconds: 3\n      periodSeconds: 5\n    livenessProbe:\n      httpGet: {path: \/, port: 80}\n      periodSeconds: 10\n      failureThreshold: 3/' /tmp/api.yaml
kubectl apply -f /tmp/api.yaml
kubectl -n probes wait --for=condition=Ready pod/api --timeout=120s
kubectl -n probes describe pod api | grep -iE "liveness|readiness"

Lab 7.5: fix removed api versions

Domain: Observability | Points: 7 | Time: about 8 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m07-05-fix-removed-api-versions)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

The directory ~/work/old holds three manifests written years ago: a CronJob report, a PodDisruptionBudget web-pdb and a Deployment web, all for the namespace legacy. kubectl apply -f ~/work/old fails because they use API versions that the cluster no longer serves. Find the correct apiVersion for each kind (for example with kubectl api-resources and kubectl explain), fix the manifests (the Deployment also needs what its current API version requires), create the namespace legacy and apply all three.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl create ns legacy
kubectl apply -f ~/work/old 2>&1 | head -5
kubectl api-resources | grep -iE "cronjobs|poddisruptionbudgets|deployments"
sed -i 's#batch/v1beta1#batch/v1#' ~/work/old/cronjob.yaml
sed -i 's#policy/v1beta1#policy/v1#' ~/work/old/pdb.yaml
sed -i 's#apps/v1beta1#apps/v1#; s#^  replicas: 2#  replicas: 2\n  selector:\n    matchLabels:\n      app: web#' ~/work/old/deployment.yaml
kubectl apply -f ~/work/old
kubectl -n legacy rollout status deployment web --timeout=120s

Lab 7.6: find api versions

Domain: Observability | Points: 5 | Time: about 5 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m07-06-find-api-versions)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

Using only kubectl against the cluster (no browser), write the current apiVersion of these four kinds to ~/answers/apis.txt, one line per kind in the form <Kind> <apiVersion>, sorted by kind name: CronJob, HorizontalPodAutoscaler, Ingress, PodDisruptionBudget.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl api-resources | head -3
for k in CronJob HorizontalPodAutoscaler Ingress PodDisruptionBudget; do
  kubectl api-resources --no-headers | awk -v k=$k '$NF==k {print k, $(NF-2)}'
done | sort > ~/answers/apis.txt
cat ~/answers/apis.txt

<!-- /LABS -->

6Recall questions

R1What does a failing readiness probe do?

Show the answer

The Pod is removed from the Service endpoints; the container is not restarted.

R2What does a failing liveness probe do?

Show the answer

The kubelet restarts the container.

R3Why add a startup probe?

Show the answer

So that a slow-starting app is not killed by the liveness probe before it has started.

R4Which probe mechanisms exist?

Show the answer

httpGet, tcpSocket, exec and grpc.

R5What status codes pass an HTTP probe?

Show the answer

200 to 399.

R6How do you find the apiVersion for a kind on your cluster?

Show the answer

kubectl api-resources | grep -i <kind> (or kubectl explain <kind>).

R7What does a removed API version produce?

Show the answer

An error such as no matches for kind ... in version ... when you apply the manifest.

R8What must you add when you change a Deployment from apps/v1beta1 to apps/v1?

Show the answer

A spec.selector that matches the Pod template labels.

Quick Reference Card

Topic Remember
Readiness not ready: out of endpoints, no restart
Liveness fails: container restarted
Startup pauses the others until it passes; failureThreshold x periodSeconds is the start budget
Mechanisms httpGet (200 to 399), tcpSocket, exec (exit 0), grpc
Defaults period 10, timeout 1, failure threshold 3, success threshold 1
Debug describe pod events, logs --previous, get endpoints
API versions api-resources, api-versions, explain; beta removed in later releases
Old manifest new apiVersion plus required fields (selector, pathType)
